About the University

The University of Greenwich is located in the Royal Borough of Greenwich in London. Its main campus is located in the iconic Old Royal Naval College, a World Heritage Site that has been seen in many movies and TV shows. The university dates back to 1891 as the Woolwich Polytechnic, eventually becoming Thames Polytechnic before gaining university status in 1992.

It appears in the top 100 UK Universities in the rankings by The Complete University Guide, The Guardian and The Times/Sunday Times. Itâ€™s also classified as Silver in Teaching Excellence Framework (TEF) of Higher Education. Around 20,000 students a year study at The University of Greenwich, including international students from more than 140 countries.

Campus Overview

The university may be primarily based in a historic building that dates back centuries, but its facilities are much more modern. New buildings and improved resources include the addition of the state-of-the-art Stockwell Street library and academic building. This Â£76-million investment is also home to the campus library, film and TV studios, and first-rate editing suites. Meanwhile, the development of the Â£25-million Dreadnought building has turned it into the central hub and a go-to place for socialisation. The neighbouring Stephen Lawrence Gallery showcases the work of contemporary artists. Greenwich Campus also has an on-site bar, two coffee shops, and several places to grab a bite.

Student Life

The campus has been heavily invested in. Two south-east London campuses in the Royal Borough of Greenwich are the iconic Old Royal Naval College in Greenwich and Avery Hill - and the historic Medway Campus in Kent. Greenwich and Avery Hill Campuses are connected by bus and train to central London. Medway Campus is just a 45-minute train journey away from the capital. The student community is close-knit and welcoming to people of all backgrounds. The student clubs are academic communities, faith spaces and hobbies. Examples include the Art Society, Desi society and Games Development club.

highlights.title: Student Life
highlights.value: The student community is close-knit and welcoming to people of all backgrounds. You can join student clubs, academic communities, and faith spaces. These include the Art Society, Desi Society, Games Development Club, and many more.

highlights.title: Accommodation
highlights.value:
International students can benefit from various cost-effective housing options at the University of Greenwich. According to The Times and The Sunday Times Good University Guide 2023, on-campus accommodation is the second cheapest in London.

Avery Hill is the most feasible accommodation option, housing over 1,200 students. The intercampus bus runs from here to the Greenwich campus until midnight throughout the week and is entirely free of charge.

The accommodation at Greenwich comprises four halls within walking distance of campus and is occupied by postgraduate students. The Medway accommodation is within walking distance of Chatham town centre, with 350 rooms on campus and options for the Medway School of Pharmacy. You can also find off-campus accommodation via the University partner, Studentpad.

Additionally, if you’re looking for budget-friendly housing options, download our app and check out the Stays feature!

highlights.title: Facilities
highlights.value:
Library
The libraries at each campus provide state-of-the-art facilities and quiet study spaces.

Sports
There are sports facilities spread across the three campuses of the university. The sports hall on the Avery Hill Campus is built for different sports, including badminton, football, basketball, netball, cricket, volleyball, and more. The campuses also hold football pitches, tennis courts and other sports facilities.

Laboratory
The University has multiple specialised lab facilities, including the Analytical Services Laboratory, TV and sound studios, and many more.

Cafeteria
You can eat or get coffee on all three campuses, including the Dreadnought Building, Queen Mary Café, the Tudor Café and the Dome, Pembroke Building, or the Pilkington Building.
